actions.text: Received in the Senate and Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
Motion to reconsider laid on the table Agreed to without objection.
On motion to suspend the rules and pass the bill Agreed to by the Yeas and Nays: (2/3 required): 373 - 14 (Roll no. 157). (text: CR H2546-2547)
Passed/agreed to in House: On motion to suspend the rules and pass the bill Agreed to by the Yeas and Nays: (2/3 required): 373 - 14 (Roll no. 157). (text: CR H2546-2547)
Considered as unfinished business. (consideration: CR H2557-2558)

At the conclusion of debate, the Yeas and Nays were demanded and ordered. Pursuant to the provisions of clause 8, rule XX, the Chair announced that further proceedings on the motion would be postponed.
DEBATE - The House proceeded with forty minutes of debate on H.R. 2035.
Considered under suspension of the rules. (consideration: CR H2546-2547)
Mr. Ezell moved to suspend the rules and pass the bill.

subcommittees.name: Coast Guard and Maritime Transportation Subcommittee

dimensions.assessment: Affects the Department of Transportation, recipients of its funding, and operators of U.S.-flagged and international commercial vessels.
dimensions.evidence: imposes the requirement on DOT (for cargo it contracts for or procures for itself) and recipients of DOT funding

dimensions.assessment: Requires a shift of ocean transport contracting up to 100% on U.S.-flagged vessels, changing shipping procedures for applicable entities.
dimensions.evidence: ensure that 100 percent of the gross tonnage of the equipment, materials, or commodities... is transported on privately-owned commercial vessels of the United States

dimensions.assessment: Modifies shipping rules for federally financed commodities, potentially affecting transport costs, but specific monetary amounts are not provided.
Amends title 46 of the United States Code to alter cargo preference mandates specifically for Department of Transportation activities and funds.
dimensions.evidence: To amend title 46, United States Code, to direct the Secretary of Transportation to ensure that all cargoes procured... are transported on privately-owned commercial vessels

dimensions.assessment: Imposes a permanent statutory requirement on applicable Department of Transportation cargo and financing.

missing_information: Financial cost estimates or exact volume of affected cargo tonnage.
importance_detail.rationale: This bill increases the cargo preference requirement from existing minimums up to 100% for Department of Transportation-procured or financed ocean transport.

card.summary: H.R. 8800 sets national defense authorizations for Fiscal Year 2027, addressing military personnel, benefits, health care, acquisition policies, military construction projects, Department of Energy national security programs, and maritime administration activities. It also includes the 'SAVE America Act', which alters federal election voting requirements.
